title: DOE UDS flow grants AES-key destination validity while writing deobfuscated material to KeyVault
claim: The DOE FSM hard-codes the UDS write_dest_valid mask to 9'h023. That mask includes bit 5, the AES-key consumer bit, so UDS-derived material is marked valid for AES consumption in addition to the intended HMAC destinations.

source_locations.excerpt: running_uds, running_fe, and running_hek are decoded from doe_cmd_reg.cmd.
The UDS branch drives kv_write.write_dest_valid as 9'h023.

security_invariant: A DOE UDS flow must not mark the resulting KeyVault entry as valid for AES-key use unless that destination is explicitly intended.

attacker_model.capability: Can initiate or influence a DOE command sequence and then rely on downstream KeyVault destination-valid metadata.
preconditions: The DOE FSM drives its KeyVault write interface.

proof_style: Directed single-DUT Verilator witness at the doe_fsm boundary.
controls: DOE_FE produces write_dest_valid=0x003, demonstrating that the harness observes the expected HMAC destination mask on a non-UDS command.
witness: DOE_UDS produces write_dest_valid=0x023, proving that destination bit 5 is asserted.
expected_evidence: proof/logs/compile.log records a single-DUT Verilator build of doe_fsm with a directed testbench.
proof/logs/run.log records BUG012_CONTROL_FE, BUG012_WITNESS, and BUG012_WITNESS_PASS.
